since 1970-01-01.\n421\t/// Returns `None` for obviously invalid inputs.\n422\tfn ymd_to_days(y: i64, m: u32, d: u32) -> Option<i64> {\n423\t    if !(1..=12).contains(&m) || !(1..=31).contains(&d) {\n424\t        return None;\n425\t    }\n426\t    // Hinnant civil_from_days inverse:\n427\t    // shift year so March = month 0\n428\t    let (y, m) = if m <= 2 { (y - 1, m + 9) } else { (y, m - 3) };\n429\t    let era = if y >= 0 { y } else { y - 399 } / 400;\n430\t    let yoe = y - era * 400; // [0, 399]\n431\t    let doy = (153 * m as i64 + 2) / 5 + d as i64 - 1; // [0, 365]\n432\t    let doe = yoe * 365 + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100 + doy; // [0, 146096]\n433\t    Some(era * 146_097 + doe - 719_468)\n434\t}\n435\t\n436\t// ── Tests ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n437\t\n438\t#[cfg(test)]\n439\tmod tests {\n440\t    use super::*;\n441\t\n442\t    /// Generate a timestamp that is guaranteed to be \"fresh\" (within the last hour)\n443\t    ///\n444\t    /// This helper creates an ISO-8601 timestamp representing a time that is\n445\t    /// 1 hour ago from the current system time. This ensures tests that check\n446\t    /// staleness with a 24-hour threshold will always see this as fresh.\n447\t    fn fresh_timestamp() -> String {\n448\t        let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()\n449\t            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n450\t            .unwrap_or_default()\n451\t            .as_secs();\n452\t\n453\t        // Go back 1 hour to ensure we're well within the 24-hour threshold\n454\t        let one_hour_ago = now.saturating_sub(3600);\n455\t\n456\t        // Convert Unix seconds back to ISO-8601\n457\t        // This is the inverse of parse_iso8601_secs\n458\t        let days_since_epoch = (one_hour_ago / 86400) as i64;\n459\t        let secs_within_day = (one_hour_ago % 86400) as u32;\n460\t\n461\t        // Convert days since epoch to YYYY-MM-DD (inverse of ymd_to_days)\n462\t        let (year, month, day) = days_to_ymd(days_since_epoch);\n463\t\n464\t        let hour = secs_within_day / 3600;\n465\t        let min = (secs_within_day % 3600) / 60;\n466\t        let sec = secs_within_day % 60;\n467\t\n468\t        format!(\"{:04}-{:02}-{:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}Z\", year, month, day, hour, min, sec)\n469\t    }\n470\t\n471\t    /// Convert days since epoch to (year, month, day)\n472\t    ///\n473\t    /// This is the inverse of ymd_to_days. For simplicity, we use a\n474\t    /// straightforward algorithm that works for dates after 1970.\n475\t    fn days_to_ymd(mut days: i64) -> (i32, u32, u32) {\n476\t        // Approximate year from days (1970 + days / 365)\n477\t        let mut year = 1970 + (days / 365) as i32;\n478\t\n479\t        // Adjust for leap years\n480\t        loop {\n481\t            let days_in_year = if is_leap_year(year) { 366 } else { 365 };\n482\t            if days < days_in_year as i64 {\n483\t                break;\n484\t            }\n485\t            days -= days_in_year as i64;\n486\t            year += 1;\n487\t        }\n488\t\n489\t        // Now 'days' is the day-of-year (0-indexed)\n490\t        let day_of_year = days as u32;\n491\t\n492\t        // Convert to month and day\n493\t        let (month, day) = day_of_year_to_md(day_of_year, year);\n494\t\n495\t        (year, month, day)\n496\t    }\n497\t\n498\t    fn is_leap_year(year: i32) -> bool {\n499\t        (year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || (year % 400 == 0)\n500\t    }\n501\t\n502\t    fn day_of_year_to_md(day_of_year: u32, year: i32) -> (u32, u32) {\n503\t        let days_in_month = if is_leap_year(year) {\n504\t            [0, 31, 29, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31]\n505\t        } else {\n506\t            [0, 31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31]\n507\t        };\n508\t\n509\t        let mut day = day_of_year + 1; // 1-indexed\n510\t        let mut month = 1;\n511\t\n512\t        while month <= 12 && day > days_in_month[month as usize] {\n513\t            day -= days_in_month[month as usize];\n514\t            month += 1;\n515\t        }\n516\t\n517\t        (month, day)\n518\t    }\n519\t\n520\t    #[test]\n521\t    fn ymd_to_days_known() {\n522\t        // 1970-01-01 = day 0\n523\t        assert_eq!(ymd_to_days(1970, 1, 1), Some(0));\n524\t        // 2000-01-01 = 10957\n525\t        assert_eq!(ymd_to_days(2000, 1, 1), Some(10957));\n526\t        // 2026-06-20 = inputs.\nfn ymd_to_days(y: i64, m: u32, d: u32) -> Option<i64> {\n    if !(1..=12).contains(&m) || !(1..=31).contains(&d) {\n        return None;\n    }\n    // Hinnant civil_from_days inverse:\n    // shift year so March = month 0\n    let (y, m) = if m <= 2 { (y - 1, m + 9) } else { (y, m - 3) };\n    let era = if y >= 0 { y } else { y - 399 } / 400;\n    let yoe = y - era * 400; // [0, 399]\n };\n\n        let mut day = day_of_year + 1; // 1-indexed\n        let mut month = 1;\n\n        while month <= 12 && day > days_in_month[month as usize] {\n            day -= days_in_month[month as Returns `false` if ANY provider has\n457\t    ///    exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n458\t    ///\n459\t    /// 3. **Re-probe condition:** Returns `false` if **EITHER** trigger fires:\n460\t    ///    - `is_stale() == true`  (probe data too old)\n461\t    ///    - `any(should_reprobe()) == true` (any provider has too many failures)\n462\t    ///\n463\t    /// This implements the OR logic for the dual-trigger system: staleness OR\n464\t    /// consecutive failures should trigger a re-probe.\n465\t    ///\n466\t    /// **Note:** This method checks staleness first (serial), then checks failures.\n467\t    /// For parallel execution of the `should_reprobe()` checks across providers,\n468\t    /// see the `ProviderProbe::is_valid()` method in `gribtract/src/provider_probe.rs`\n469\t    /// which uses `par_iter().any()` for concurrent checking.\n470\t    ///\n471\t    /// This is a convenience method that combines the staleness check with the\n472\t    /// failure tracker check. Returns true if the probe results are fresh AND\n473\t    /// no tracked providers have exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n474\t    ///\n475\t    /// # Arguments\n476\t    /// * `results` - The probe results to check for staleness\n477\t    /// * `max_age` - Maximum age for probe results to be considered fresh\n478\t    ///\n479\t    /// # Example\n480\t    /// ```no_run\n481\t    /// use gribtract_fetch::probe::ProviderProbe;\n482\t    /// use std::time::Duration;\n483\t    ///\n484\t    /// let probe = ProviderProbe::new();\n485\t    /// let results = ProviderProbe::load_results(std::path::Path::new(\"provider-probe.json\")).unwrap();\n486\t    ///\n487\t    /// // Check if results are valid (fresh AND no providers need re-probing)\n488\t    /// if !probe.is_valid(&results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)) {\n489\t    ///     // Trigger re-probe...\n490\t    /// }\n491\t    /// ```\n492\t    pub fn is_valid(&self, results: &ProviderProbeResults, max_age: Duration) -> bool {\n493\t        // First check staleness\n494\t        if Self::is_stale(results, max_age) {\n495\t            return false;\n496\t        }\n497\t\n498\t        // Then check if any tracked provider has exceeded the failure threshold\n499\t        // Use should_reprobe() for consistency\n500\t        //\n501\t        // INTEGRATION: This is where should_reprobe() is called to implement the\n502\t        // failure-tracking half of the dual-trigger re-probe logic.\n503\t        for provider in self.consecutive_failures.keys() {\n504\t            if self.should_reprobe(provider) {\n505\t                return false;\n506\t            }\n507\t        }\n508\t\n509\t        true\n510\t    }\n511\t\n512\t    /// Get providers that need re-probing due to consecutive failures\n513\t    ///\n514\t    /// Returns a list of provider names that have exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n515\t    /// This can be used to log which providers are problematic before triggering a re-probe.\n516\t    ///\n517\t    /// # Returns\n518\t    /// A vector of provider names that need re-probing\n519\t    pub fn providers_needing_reprobe(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n520\t        let mut needing = Vec::new();\n521\t\n522\t        for (provider, &count) in &self.consecutive_failures {\n523\t            if count >= self.consecutive_failure_threshold {\n524\t                needing.push(provider.clone());\n525\t            }\n526\t        }\n527\t\n528\t        needing\n529\t    }\n530\t\n531\t    /// Get the current consecutive failure count for a provider\n532\t    pub fn failure_count(&self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n533\t        self.consecutive_failures.get(provider).copied().unwrap_or(0)\n534\t    }\n535\t\n536\t    /// Get the consecutive failure threshold\n537\t    pub fn failure_threshold(&self) -> u32 {\n538\t        self.consecutive_failure_threshold\n539\t    }\n540\t\n541\t    /// Reset all failure counters\n542\t    pub fn reset_failures(&mut self) {\n543\t        self.consecutive_failures.clear();\n544\t    }\n545\t}\n546\t\n547\timpl Default for ProviderProbe {\n548\t    fn default() -> Self {\n549\t        Self::new()\n550\t    }\n551\t}\n552\t\n553\t/// Inner result from a single probe\n554\t#[derive(Debug)]\n555\tstruct ProbeInnerResult {\n556\t    connect_time: Duration,\n557\t    ttfb: Duration,\n558\t    throughput_mbs: f64,\n559\t}\n560\t\n561\t/// Runtime tracker for consecutive provider failures\n562\t///\n563\t/// This is a lightweight struct that can be used at runtime to track HTTP request\n564\t/// failures per provider and determine when re-probing is needed. It should be used\n565\t/// alongside the loaded provider-probe.json results.\n566\t///\n567\t/// # Example\n568\t///\n569\t/// This example shows how to use the failure tracker to monitor provider health:\n570\t///\n571\t/// ```no_run\n572\t/// use gribtract_fetch::probe::ProviderFailureTracker;\n573\t///\n574\t/// // Create a failure tracker with threshold of 3 consecutive errors\n575\t/// let mut tracker = ProviderFailureTracker::new(3);\n576\t///\n577\t/// // Simulate HTTP request results\n578\t/// // tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n579\t/// // tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n580\t/// // tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n581\t///\n582\t/// // Check if re-probing is needed\n583\t/// if tracker.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\") {\n584\t///     println!(\"Provider s3:hrrr needs re-probing due to consecutive failures\");\n585\t/// }\n586\t///\n587\t/// // Reset after successful request\n588\t/// // tracker.record_success(\"s3:hrrr\");\n589\t/// ```\n590\t#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n591\tpub struct ProviderFailureTracker {\n592\t    /// Consecutive failure count per provider\n593\t    failures: std::collections::HashMap<String, u32>,\n594\t    /// Threshold for consecutive failures before re-probing\n595\t    threshold: u32,\n596\t}\n597\t\n598\timpl ProviderFailureTracker {\n599\t    /// Create a new failure tracker with the specified threshold\n600\t    pub fn new(threshold: u32) -> Self {\n601\t        Self {\n602\t            failures: std::collections::HashMap::new(),\n603\t            threshold,\n604\t        }\n605\t    }\n606\t\n607\t    /// Create a new failure tracker with default threshold (3)\n608\t    pub fn default_threshold() -> Self {\n609\t        Self::new(3)\n610\t    }\n611\t\n612\t    /// Record a failure for the given provider\n613\t    ///\n614\t    /// Returns the current failure count after incrementing.\n615\t    pub fn record_failure(&mut self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n616\t        let count = self.failures.entry(provider.to_string()).or_insert(0);\n617\t        *count += 1;\n618\t        *count\n619\t    }\n620\t\n621\t    /// Record a success for the given provider\n622\t    ///\n623\t    /// Resets the consecutive failure counter for the provider to zero.\n624\t    pub fn record_success(&mut self, provider: &str) {\n625\t        self.failures.insert(provider.to_string(), 0);\n626\t    }\n627\t\n628\t    /// Check if a provider should be re-probed due to consecutive failures\n629\t    ///\n630\t    /// Returns true if the provider has exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n631\t    /// This should be checked alongside the staleness check when deciding whether\n632\t    /// to refresh provider probe results.\n633\t    pub fn should_reprobe(&self, provider: &str) -> bool {\n634\t        self.failures\n635\t            .get(provider)\n636\t            .map(|&count| count >= self.threshold)\n637\t            .unwrap_or(false)\n638\t    }\n639\t\n640\t    /// Get the current consecutive failure count for a provider\n641\t    pub fn failure_count(&self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n642\t        self.failures.get(provider).copied().unwrap_or(0)\n643\t    }\n644\t\n645\t    /// Get the consecutive failure threshold\n646\t    pub fn threshold(&self) -> u32 {\n647\t        self.threshold\n648\t    }\n649\t\n650\t    /// Reset all failure counters (e.g., after re-probing completes)\n651\t    pub fn reset_all(&mut self) {\n652\t        self.failures.clear();\n653\t    }\n654\t\n655\t    /// Reset failure counter for a specific provider\n656\t    pub fn reset_provider(&mut self, provider: &str) {\n657\t        self.failures.insert(provider.to_string(), 0);\n658\t    }\n659\t}\n660\t\n661\t#[cfg(test)]\n662\tmod failure_tracker_tests {\n663\t    use super::*;\n664\t\n665\t    #[test]\n666\t    fn test_failure_tracker_basic() {\n667\t        let mut tracker =  // Collect the models and probe_files to avoid borrow checker issues\n        let models: Vec<(String, Vec<(String, String)>)> = self.probe_files\n            .iter()\n            .map(|(model,  Ok(result) => {\n                let _elapsed = start.elapsed();\n                ProbeResult {\n                    provider: provider.to_string(),\n                    probe_url: url.to_string(),\n std::time::Instant::now();\n\n        // Use the client's probe method to get basic connection info\n        let probe_info = self.client.probe(url).await?;\n        let connect_time = probe_info.connect_time;\n\n        // Check if range requests are supported\n        let supports_range = probe_info.supports_range;\n\n        // Get content length\n        let content_length = probe_info.content_length.unwrap_or(0);\n\n        // Now do a small range request to measure TTFB and throughput\n        let range_start = std::time::Instant::now();\n\n        let range_response = if supports_range && content_length > 1024 {\n            Some(self.client.fetch_head(url, 1024).await?)\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        let ttfb = range_start.elapsed();\n\n        let throughput_mbs = if let Some(resp) = range_response {\n            let bytes = resp.data.len() as f64;\n            let seconds = ttfb.as_secs_f64();\n            (bytes / seconds) / (1024.0 * 1024.0)\n        } else {\n            0.0\n        };\n\n        Ok(ProbeInnerResult {\n            connect_time,\n            ttfb,\n            throughput_mbs,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Calculate a combined score for provider selection\n    ///\n    /// Lower is better. Formula: connect_ms + ttfb_ms + (1 / throughput_mbs)\n    fn calculate_score(result: &ProbeInnerResult) -> f64 {\n        let connect_penalty = result.connect_time.as_millis() as f64;\n        let ttfb_penalty = result.ttfb.as_millis() as f64;\n        let throughput_penalty = if result.throughput_mbs > 0.0 {\n            1000.0 / result.throughput_mbs\n        } else {\n            10000.0 // Large penalty for no throughput\n        };\n\n        connect_penalty + ttfb_penalty + throughput_penalty\n    }\n\n    /// Get the current git SHA for reproducibility\n    fn get_git_sha() -> Option<String> {\n        std::process::Command::new(\"git\")\n            .args([\"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\"])\n            .output()\n            .ok()\n            .and_then(|output| {\n                let sha = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();\n                if !sha.is_empty() {\n                    Some(sha)\n                } else {\n                    None\n                }\n            })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the best provider for a model based on probe results\n    ///\n    /// This version does NOT check the failure tracker. Use `get_best_provider_with_tracker()`\n    /// to skip providers that need re-probing due to consecutive failures.\n    pub fn get_best_provider<'a>(\n        results: &'a ProviderProbeResults,\n        model: &str,\n    ) -> Option<&'a ProbeResult> {\n        results.models.get(model).and_then(|model_results| {\n            model_results.iter().find(|r| r.success)\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the best provider for a model that does NOT need re-probing\n    ///\n    /// # INTEGRATION POINT: should_reprobe + Provider Selection\n    ///\n    /// This is the **primary integration point** where `should_reprobe()` is called\n    /// during runtime provider selection. The integration works as follows:\n    ///\n    /// 1. **Parallel execution:** Uses `par_iter()` via rayon to check `should_reprobe()`\n    ///    for all provider candidates **concurrently**, improving performance when\n    ///    there are multiple providers to evaluate.\n    ///\n    /// 2. **Dual-trigger logic:** Combined with `is_stale()` in `is_valid()` method,\n    ///    this implements the dual-trigger re-probe mechanism:\n    ///    - Staleness trigger: `is_stale()` returns true if probe data > 24h old\n    ///    - Failure trigger: `should_reprobe()` returns true if failures >= threshold\n    ///    - Re-probe if **EITHER** trigger fires (OR logic, not AND)\n    ///\n    /// 3. **Data flow:**\n    ///    - HTTP requests → automatic failure/success recording in `FetchClient`\n    ///    - `consecutive_failures` HashMap tracks failures per provider\n    ///    - `should_reprobe()` checks: `failures.get(provider) >= threshold`\n    ///    - This method skips providers where `should_reprobe() == true`\n    ///\n    /// 4. **Expected behavior:** Per design requirements, `should_reprobe()` runs in\n    ///    parallel across all provider candidates (not parallel with `is_stale()`, which\n    ///    is checked once globally before this method is called).\n    ///\n    /// Returns the first successful provider in the results that has not exceeded the\n    /// consecutive failure threshold. This should be used during runtime provider selection\n    /// to ensure we don't select providers that are experiencing repeated failures.\n    ///\n    /// Uses parallel execution (via rayon) to check `should_reprobe()` for all providers\n    /// concurrently, improving performance when there are multiple providers to evaluate.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `results` - The probe results to select from\n    /// * `model` - The model to get the best provider for (e.g., \"hrrr\", \"gefs\", \"nbm\", \"gfs\")\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `Some(&ProbeResult)` - The best provider result that doesn't need re-probing\n    /// * `None` - If all providers need re-probing or the model doesn't exist\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use gribtract_fetch::probe::{ProviderProbe, ProviderProbeResults};\n    ///\n    /// let mut probe = ProviderProbe::new();\n    /// let results = ProviderProbe::load_results(std::path::Path::new(\"provider-probe.json\")).unwrap();\n    ///\n    /// // Get the best provider that isn't experiencing repeated failures\n    /// if let Some(best) = probe.get_best_provider_with_tracker(&results, \"hrrr\") {\n    ///     println!(\"Best HRRR provider: {} (score: {:.1})\", best.provider, best.score);\n    /// }\n    /// ```\n    #[cfg(feature = \"rayon\")]\n    pub fn get_best_provider_with_tracker<'a>(\n        &'a self,\n        results: &'a ProviderProbeResults,\n        model: &str,\n    ) -> Option<&'a ProbeResult> {\n        use rayon::prelude::*;\n\n        results.models.get(model).and_then(|model_results| {\n            // Parallel iteration over provider results\n            // Find the first successful provider that doesn't need re-probing\n            //\n            // INTEGRATION: This is where should_reprobe() is called during provider selection.\n            // The par_iter() ensures all providers are checked concurrently for efficiency.\n            model_results.par_iter().find_any(|r| {\n                r.success && !self.should_reprobe(&r.provider)\n            }).or_else(|| {\n                // Fallback: if all providers need re-probing, return the first successful one\n                model_results.iter().find(|r| r.success)\n            })\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the best provider for a model that does NOT need re-probing (synchronous version)\n    ///\n    /// This is a synchronous version of `get_best_provider_with_tracker` that does not\n    /// use parallel execution. It's available when the `rayon` feature is not enabled.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `results` - The probe results to select from\n    /// * `model` - The model to get the best provider for\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `Some(&ProbeResult)` - The best provider result that doesn't need re-probing\n    /// * `None` - If all providers need re-probing or the model doesn't exist\n    #[cfg(not(feature = \"rayon\"))]\n    pub fn get_best_provider_with_tracker<'a>(\n        &'a self,\n        results: &'a ProviderProbeResults,\n        model: &str,\n    ) -> Option<&'a ProbeResult> {\n        results.models.get(model).and_then(|model_results| {\n            model_results.iter().find(|r| {\n                r.success && !self.should_reprobe(&r.provider)\n            })\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Write probe results to a JSON file\n    pub fn write_results(results: &ProviderProbeResults, path: &std::path::Path) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n        let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(results)?;\n        std::fs::write(path, json)\n    }\n\n    /// Load probe results from a JSON file\n    pub fn load_results(path: &std::path::Path) ->  /// Check if probe results are stale (older than 24 hours)\n    pub fn is_stale(results: &ProviderProbeResults, max_age: Duration) -> bool {\n        match chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&results.timestamp) {\n            Ok(timestamp) => {\n                let now = chrono::Utc::now();\n                let age = now.signed_duration_since(timestamp);\n                age.to_std().unwrap_or(Duration::ZERO) > max_age\n            }\n            Err(_) => true, // Invalid timestamp means stale\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a failure for the given provider\n    ///\n    /// Increments the consecutive failure counter for the provider.\n    /// Returns the current failure count after incrementing.\n    pub fn record_failure(&mut self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n        let count = self.consecutive_failures.entry(provider.to_string()).or_insert(0);\n        *count += 1;\n        *count\n    }\n\n    /// Record a success for the given provider\n    ///\n    /// Resets the consecutive failure counter for the provider to zero.\n    pub fn record_success(&mut self, provider: &str) {\n        self.consecutive_failures.insert(provider.to_string(), 0);\n    }\n\n    /// Check if a provider should be re-probed due to consecutive failures\n    ///\n    /// Returns true if the provider has exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    /// This should be checked alongside the staleness check when deciding whether\n    /// to refresh provider probe results.\n    pub fn should_reprobe(&self, provider: &str) -> bool {\n        self.consecutive_failures\n            .get(provider)\n            .map(|&count| count >= self.consecutive_failure_threshold)\n            .unwrap_or(false)\n    }\n\n    /// Check if probe results are valid (fresh AND no providers need re-probing)\n    ///\n    /// # INTEGRATION POINT: Dual-Trigger Re-probe Logic (is_stale + should_reprobe)\n    ///\n    /// This is the **secondary integration point** where staleness checking and\n    /// failure tracking are combined to determine if re-probing is needed.\n    ///\n    /// **Dual-trigger logic:**\n    /// 1. **Staleness trigger:** Calls `is_stale()` (lines 374-384) to check if\n    ///    probe data is older than `max_age` (default 24 hours). Returns `false`\n    ///    immediately if stale.\n    ///\n    /// 2. **Failure trigger:** Iterates over all tracked providers and calls\n    ///    `should_reprobe()` for each. Returns `false` if ANY provider has\n    ///    exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    ///\n    /// 3. **Re-probe condition:** Returns `false` if **EITHER** trigger fires:\n    ///    - `is_stale() == true`  (probe data too old)\n    ///    - `any(should_reprobe()) == true` (any provider has too many failures)\n    ///\n    /// This implements the OR logic for the dual-trigger system: staleness OR\n    /// consecutive failures should trigger a re-probe.\n    ///\n    /// **Note:** This method checks staleness first (serial), then checks failures.\n    /// For parallel execution of the `should_reprobe()` checks across providers,\n    /// see the `ProviderProbe::is_valid()` method in `gribtract/src/provider_probe.rs`\n    /// which uses `par_iter().any()` for concurrent checking.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method that combines the staleness check with the\n    /// failure tracker check. Returns true if the probe results are fresh AND\n    /// no tracked providers have exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `results` - The probe results to check for staleness\n    /// * `max_age` - Maximum age for probe results to be considered fresh\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use gribtract_fetch::probe::ProviderProbe;\n    /// use std::time::Duration;\n    ///\n    /// let probe = ProviderProbe::new();\n    /// let results = ProviderProbe::load_results(std::path::Path::new(\"provider-probe.json\")).unwrap();\n    ///\n    /// // Check if results are valid (fresh AND no providers need re-probing)\n    /// if !probe.is_valid(&results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)) {\n    ///     // Trigger re-probe...\n    /// }\n    /// ```\n    pub fn is_valid(&self, results: &ProviderProbeResults, max_age: Duration) -> bool {\n        // First check staleness\n        if Self::is_stale(results, max_age) {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Then check if any tracked provider has exceeded the failure threshold\n        // Use should_reprobe() for consistency\n        //\n        // INTEGRATION: This is where should_reprobe() is called to implement the\n        // failure-tracking half of the dual-trigger re-probe logic.\n        for provider in self.consecutive_failures.keys() {\n            if self.should_reprobe(provider) {\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n\n        true\n    }\n\n    /// Get providers that need re-probing due to consecutive failures\n    ///\n    /// Returns a list of provider names that have exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    /// This can be used to log which providers are problematic before triggering a re-probe.\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// A vector of provider names that need re-probing\n    pub fn providers_needing_reprobe(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        let mut needing = Vec::new();\n\n        for (provider, &count) in &self.consecutive_failures {\n            if count >= self.consecutive_failure_threshold {\n                needing.push(provider.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        needing\n    }\n\n    /// Get the current consecutive failure count for a provider\n    pub fn failure_count(&self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n        self.consecutive_failures.get(provider).copied().unwrap_or(0)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the consecutive failure threshold\n    pub fn failure_threshold(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.consecutive_failure_threshold\n    }\n\n    /// Reset all failure counters\n    pub fn reset_failures(&mut self) {\n        self.consecutive_failures.clear();\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for ProviderProbe {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Inner result from a single probe\n#[derive(Debug)]\nstruct ProbeInnerResult {\n    connect_time: Duration,\n    ttfb: Duration,\n    throughput_mbs: f64,\n}\n\n/// Runtime tracker for consecutive provider failures\n///\n/// This is a lightweight struct that can be used at runtime to track HTTP request\n/// failures per provider and determine when re-probing is needed. It should be used\n/// alongside the loaded provider-probe.json results.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// This example shows how to use the failure tracker to monitor provider health:\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use gribtract_fetch::probe::ProviderFailureTracker;\n///\n/// // Create a failure tracker with threshold of 3 consecutive errors\n/// let mut tracker = ProviderFailureTracker::new(3);\n///\n/// // Simulate HTTP request results\n/// // tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n/// // tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n/// // tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n///\n/// // Check if re-probing is needed\n/// if tracker.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\") {\n///     println!(\"Provider s3:hrrr needs re-probing due to consecutive failures\");\n/// }\n///\n/// // Reset after successful request\n/// // tracker.record_success(\"s3:hrrr\");\n/// ```\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ProviderFailureTracker {\n    /// Consecutive failure count per provider\n    failures: std::collections::HashMap<String, u32>,\n    /// Threshold for consecutive failures before re-probing\n    threshold: u32,\n}\n\nimpl ProviderFailureTracker {\n    /// Create a new failure tracker with the specified threshold\n    pub fn new(threshold: u32) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            failures: std::collections::HashMap::new(),\n            threshold,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new failure tracker with default threshold (3)\n    pub fn default_threshold() -> Self {\n        Self::new(3)\n    }\n\n    /// Record a failure for the given provider\n    ///\n    /// Returns the current failure count after incrementing.\n    pub fn record_failure(&mut self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n        let count = self.failures.entry(provider.to_string()).or_insert(0);\n        *count += 1;\n        *count\n    }\n\n    /// Record a success for the given provider\n    ///\n    /// Resets the consecutive failure counter for the provider to zero.\n    pub fn record_success(&mut self, provider: &str) {\n        self.failures.insert(provider.to_string(), 0);\n    }\n\n    /// Check if a provider should be re-probed due to consecutive failures\n    ///\n    /// Returns true if the provider has exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    /// This should be checked alongside the staleness check when deciding whether\n    /// to refresh provider probe results.\n    pub fn should_reprobe(&self, provider: &str) -> bool {\n        self.failures\n            .get(provider)\n            .map(|&count| count >= self.threshold)\n            .unwrap_or(false)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the current consecutive failure count for a provider\n    pub fn failure_count(&self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n        self.failures.get(provider).copied().unwrap_or(0)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the consecutive failure threshold\n    pub fn threshold(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.threshold\n    }\n\n    /// Reset all failure counters (e.g., after re-probing completes)\n    pub fn reset_all(&mut self) {\n        self.failures.clear();\n    }\n\n    /// Reset failure counter for a specific provider\n    pub fn reset_provider(&mut self, provider: &str) {\n        self.failures.insert(provider.to_string(), 0);\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod failure_tracker_tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn     assert!(!tracker.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\"));\n\n        // Record first failure\n        assert_eq!(tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\"), 1);\n        assert_eq!(tracker.failure_count(\"s3:hrrr\"), 1);\n        assert!(!tracker.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\"));\n\n        // Record second failure\n        assert_eq!(tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\"), assert_eq!(tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\"), 3);\n        assert_eq!(tracker.failure_count(\"s3:hrrr\"), 3);\n        assert!(tracker.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\"));\n\n        // Record a success - range_start.elapsed();\n\n        let throughput_mbs = if let Some(resp) = range_response {\n            let bytes = resp.data.len() as f64;\n            let seconds = ttfb.as_secs_f64();\n            (bytes / seconds) / (1024.0 * 1024.0)\n        } else {\n            0.0\n        };\n\n        Ok(ProbeInnerResult {\n            connect_time,\n            ttfb,\n            throughput_mbs,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Calculate a combined score for provider selection\n    ///\n    /// Lower is better. Formula: connect_ms + ttfb_ms + (1 / throughput_mbs)\n    fn calculate_score(result: &ProbeInnerResult) -> f64 {\n        let connect_penalty = result.connect_time.as_millis() as f64;\n        let ttfb_penalty = result.ttfb.as_millis() as f64;\n        let throughput_penalty = if result.throughput_mbs > 0.0 {\n            1000.0 / result.throughput_mbs\n        } else {\n            10000.0 // Large penalty for no throughput\n        };\n\n        connect_penalty + ttfb_penalty + throughput_penalty\n    }\n\n    /// Get the current git SHA for reproducibility\n    fn get_git_sha() -> Option<String> {\n        std::process::Command::new(\"git\")\n            .args([\"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\"])\n            .output()\n            .ok()\n            .and_then(|output| {\n                let sha = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();\n                if !sha.is_empty() {\n                    Some(sha)\n                } else {\n                    None\n                }\n            })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the best provider for a model based on probe results\n    ///\n    /// This version does NOT check the failure tracker. Use `get_best_provider_with_tracker()`\n    /// to skip providers that need re-probing due to consecutive failures.\n    pub fn get_best_provider<'a>(\n        results: &'a ProviderProbeResults,\n        model: &str,\n    ) -> Option<&'a ProbeResult> {\n        results.models.get(model).and_then(|model_results| {\n            model_results.iter().find(|r| r.success)\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the best provider for a model that does NOT need re-probing\n    ///\n    /// # INTEGRATION POINT: should_reprobe + Provider Selection\n    ///\n    /// This is the **primary integration point** where `should_reprobe()` is called\n    /// during runtime provider selection. The integration works as follows:\n    ///\n    /// 1. **Parallel execution:** Uses `par_iter()` via rayon to check `should_reprobe()`\n    ///    for all provider candidates **concurrently**, improving performance when\n    ///    there are multiple providers to evaluate.\n    ///\n    /// 2. **Dual-trigger logic:** Combined with `is_stale()` in `is_valid()` method,\n    ///    this implements the dual-trigger re-probe mechanism:\n    ///    - Staleness trigger: `is_stale()` returns true if probe data > 24h old\n    ///    - Failure trigger: `should_reprobe()` returns true if failures >= threshold\n    ///    - Re-probe if **EITHER** trigger fires (OR logic, not AND)\n    ///\n    /// 3. **Data flow:**\n    ///    - HTTP requests → automatic failure/success recording in `FetchClient`\n    ///    - `consecutive_failures` HashMap tracks failures per provider\n    ///    - `should_reprobe()` checks: `failures.get(provider) >= threshold`\n    ///    - This method skips providers where `should_reprobe() == true`\n    ///\n    /// 4. **Expected behavior:** Per design requirements, `should_reprobe()` runs in\n    ///    parallel across all provider candidates (not parallel with `is_stale()`, which\n    ///    is checked once globally before this method is called).\n    ///\n    /// Returns the first successful provider in the results that has not exceeded the\n    /// consecutive failure threshold. This should be used during runtime provider selection\n    /// to ensure we don't select providers that are experiencing repeated failures.\n    ///\n    /// Uses parallel execution (via rayon) to check `should_reprobe()` for all providers\n    /// concurrently, improving performance when there are multiple providers to evaluate.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `results` - The probe results to select from\n    /// * `model` - The model to get the best provider for (e.g., \"hrrr\", \"gefs\", \"nbm\", \"gfs\")\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `Some(&ProbeResult)` - The best provider result that doesn't need re-probing\n    /// * `None` - If all providers need re-probing or the model doesn't exist\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use gribtract_fetch::probe::{ProviderProbe, ProviderProbeResults};\n    ///\n    /// let mut probe = ProviderProbe::new();\n    /// let results = ProviderProbe::load_results(std::path::Path::new(\"provider-probe.json\")).unwrap();\n    ///\n    /// // Get the best provider that isn't experiencing repeated failures\n    /// if let Some(best) = probe.get_best_provider_with_tracker(&results, \"hrrr\") {\n    ///     println!(\"Best HRRR provider: {} (score: {:.1})\", best.provider, best.score);\n    /// }\n    /// ```\n    #[cfg(feature = \"rayon\")]\n    pub fn get_best_provider_with_tracker<'a>(\n        &'a self,\n        results: &'a ProviderProbeResults,\n        model: &str,\n    ) -> Option<&'a ProbeResult> {\n        use rayon::prelude::*;\n\n        results.models.get(model).and_then(|model_results| {\n            // Parallel iteration over provider results\n            // Find the first successful provider that doesn't need re-probing\n            //\n            // INTEGRATION: This is where should_reprobe() is called during provider selection.\n            // The par_iter() ensures all providers are checked concurrently for efficiency.\n            model_results.par_iter().find_any(|r| {\n                r.success && !self.should_reprobe(&r.provider)\n            }).or_else(|| {\n                // Fallback: if all providers need re-probing, return the first successful one\n                model_results.iter().find(|r| r.success)\n            })\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the best provider for a model that does NOT need re-probing (synchronous version)\n    ///\n    /// This is a synchronous version of `get_best_provider_with_tracker` that does not\n    /// use parallel execution. It's available when the `rayon` feature is not enabled.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `results` - The probe results to select from\n    /// * `model` - The model to get the best provider for\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `Some(&ProbeResult)` - The best provider result that doesn't need re-probing\n    /// * `None` - If all providers need re-probing or the model doesn't exist\n    #[cfg(not(feature = \"rayon\"))]\n    pub fn get_best_provider_with_tracker<'a>(\n        &'a self,\n        results: &'a ProviderProbeResults,\n        model: &str,\n    ) -> Option<&'a ProbeResult> {\n        results.models.get(model).and_then(|model_results| {\n            model_results.iter().find(|r| {\n                r.success && !self.should_reprobe(&r.provider)\n            })\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Write probe results to a JSON file\n    pub fn write_results(results: &ProviderProbeResults, path: &std::path::Path) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n        let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(results)?;\n        std::fs::write(path, json)\n    }\n\n    /// Load probe results from a JSON file\n    pub fn load_results(path: &std::path::Path) -> std::io::Result<ProviderProbeResults> {\n        let json = std::fs::read_to_string(path)?;\n        let results: ProviderProbeResults = serde_json::from_str(&json)?;\n        Ok(results)\n    }\n\n    /// Check if probe results are stale (older than 24 hours)\n    pub fn is_stale(results: &ProviderProbeResults, max_age: Duration) -> bool {\n        match chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&results.timestamp) {\n            Ok(timestamp) => {\n                let now = chrono::Utc::now();\n                let age = now.signed_duration_since(timestamp);\n                age.to_std().unwrap_or(Duration::ZERO) > max_age\n            }\n            Err(_) => true, // Invalid timestamp means stale\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a failure for the given provider\n    ///\n    /// Increments the consecutive failure counter for the provider.\n    /// Returns the current failure count after incrementing.\n    pub fn record_failure(&mut self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n        let count = self.consecutive_failures.entry(provider.to_string()).or_insert(0);\n        *count += 1;\n        *count\n    }\n\n    /// Record a success for the given provider\n    ///\n    /// Resets the consecutive failure counter for the provider to zero.\n    pub fn record_success(&mut self, provider: &str) {\n        self.consecutive_failures.insert(provider.to_string(), 0);\n    }\n\n    /// Check if a provider should be re-probed due to consecutive failures\n    ///\n    /// Returns true if the provider has exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    /// This should be checked alongside the staleness check when deciding whether\n    /// to refresh provider probe results.\n    pub fn should_reprobe(&self, provider: &str) -> bool {\n        self.consecutive_failures\n            .get(provider)\n            .map(|&count| count >= self.consecutive_failure_threshold)\n            .unwrap_or(false)\n    }\n\n    /// Check if probe results are valid (fresh AND no providers need re-probing)\n    ///\n    /// # INTEGRATION POINT: Dual-Trigger Re-probe Logic (is_stale + should_reprobe)\n    ///\n    /// This is the **secondary integration point** where staleness checking and\n    /// failure tracking are combined to determine if re-probing is needed.\n    ///\n    /// **Dual-trigger logic:**\n    /// 1. **Staleness trigger:** Calls `is_stale()` (lines 374-384) to check if\n    ///    probe data is older than `max_age` (default 24 hours). Returns `false`\n    ///    immediately if stale.\n    ///\n    /// 2. **Failure trigger:** Iterates over all tracked providers and calls\n    ///    `should_reprobe()` for each. Returns `false` if ANY provider has\n    ///    exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    ///\n    /// 3. **Re-probe condition:** Returns `false` if **EITHER** trigger fires:\n    ///    - `is_stale() == true`  (probe data too old)\n    ///    - `any(should_reprobe()) == true` (any provider has too many failures)\n    ///\n    /// This implements the OR logic for the dual-trigger system: staleness OR\n    /// consecutive failures should trigger a re-probe.\n    ///\n    /// **Note:** This method checks staleness first (serial), then checks failures.\n    /// For parallel execution of the `should_reprobe()` checks across providers,\n    /// see the `ProviderProbe::is_valid()` method in `gribtract/src/provider_probe.rs`\n    /// which uses `par_iter().any()` for concurrent checking.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method that combines the staleness check with the\n    /// failure tracker check. Returns true if the probe results are fresh AND\n    /// no tracked providers have exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `results` - The probe results to check for staleness\n    /// * `max_age` - Maximum age for probe results to be considered fresh\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use gribtract_fetch::probe::ProviderProbe;\n    /// use std::time::Duration;\n    ///\n    /// let probe = ProviderProbe::new();\n    /// let results = ProviderProbe::load_results(std::path::Path::new(\"provider-probe.json\")).unwrap();\n    ///\n    /// // Check if results are valid (fresh AND no providers need re-probing)\n    /// if !probe.is_valid(&results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)) {\n    ///     // Trigger re-probe...\n    /// }\n    /// ```\n    pub fn is_valid(&self, results: &ProviderProbeResults, max_age: Duration) -> bool {\n        // First check staleness\n        if Self::is_stale(results, max_age) {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Then check if any tracked provider has exceeded the failure threshold\n        // Use should_reprobe() for consistency\n        //\n        // INTEGRATION: This is where should_reprobe() is called to implement the\n        // failure-tracking half of the dual-trigger re-probe logic.\n        for provider in self.consecutive_failures.keys() {\n            if self.should_reprobe(provider) {\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n\n        true\n    }\n\n    /// Get providers that need re-probing due to consecutive failures\n    ///\n    /// Returns a list of provider names that have exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    /// This can be used to log which providers are problematic before triggering a re-probe.\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// A vector of provider names that need re-probing\n    pub fn providers_needing_reprobe(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        let mut needing = Vec::new();\n\n        for (provider, &count) in &self.consecutive_failures {\n            if count >= self.consecutive_failure_threshold {\n                needing.push(provider.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        needing\n    }\n\n    /// Get the current consecutive failure count for a provider\n    pub fn failure_count(&self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n        self.consecutive_failures.get(provider).copied().unwrap_or(0)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the consecutive failure threshold\n    pub fn failure_threshold(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.consecutive_failure_threshold\n    }\n\n    /// Reset all failure counters\n    pub fn reset_failures(&mut self) {\n        self.consecutive_failures.clear();\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for ProviderProbe {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Inner result from a single probe\n#[derive(Debug)]\nstruct ProbeInnerResult {\n    connect_time: Duration,\n    ttfb: Duration,\n    throughput_mbs: f64,\n}\n\n/// Runtime tracker for consecutive provider failures\n///\n/// This is a lightweight struct that can be used at runtime to track HTTP request\n/// failures per provider and determine when re-probing is needed. It should be used\n/// alongside the loaded provider-probe.json results.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// This example shows how to use the failure tracker to monitor provider health:\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use gribtract_fetch::probe::ProviderFailureTracker;\n///\n/// // Create a failure tracker with threshold of 3 consecutive errors\n/// let mut tracker = ProviderFailureTracker::new(3);\n///\n/// // Simulate HTTP request results\n/// // tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n/// // tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n/// // tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n///\n/// // Check if re-probing is needed\n/// if tracker.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\") {\n///     println!(\"Provider s3:hrrr needs re-probing due to consecutive failures\");\n/// }\n///\n/// // Reset after successful request\n/// // tracker.record_success(\"s3:hrrr\");\n/// ```\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ProviderFailureTracker {\n    /// Consecutive failure count per provider\n    failures: std::collections::HashMap<String, u32>,\n    /// Threshold for consecutive failures before re-probing\n    threshold: u32,\n}\n\nimpl ProviderFailureTracker {\n    /// Create a new failure tracker with the specified threshold\n    pub fn new(threshold: u32) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            failures: std::collections::HashMap::new(),\n            threshold,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new failure tracker with default threshold (3)\n    pub fn default_threshold() -> Self {\n        Self::new(3)\n    }\n\n    /// Record a failure for the given provider\n    ///\n    /// Returns the current failure count after incrementing.\n    pub fn record_failure(&mut self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n        let count = self.failures.entry(provider.to_string()).or_insert(0);\n        *count += 1;\n        *count\n    }\n\n    /// Record a success for the given provider\n    ///\n    /// Resets the consecutive failure counter for the provider to zero.\n    pub fn record_success(&mut self, provider: &str) {\n        self.failures.insert(provider.to_string(), 0);\n    }\n\n    /// Check if a provider should be re-probed due to consecutive failures\n    ///\n    /// Returns true if the provider has exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    /// This should be checked alongside the staleness check when deciding whether\n    /// to refresh provider probe results.\n    pub fn should_reprobe(&self, provider: &str) -> bool {\n        self.failures\n            .get(provider)\n            .map(|&count| count >= self.threshold)\n            .unwrap_or(false)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the current consecutive failure count for a provider\n    pub fn failure_count(&self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n        self.failures.get(provider).copied().unwrap_or(0)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the consecutive failure threshold\n    pub fn threshold(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.threshold\n    }\n\n    /// Reset all failure counters (e.g., after re-probing completes)\n    pub fn reset_all(&mut self) {\n        self.failures.clear();\n    }\n\n    /// Reset failure counter for a specific provider\n    pub fn reset_provider(&mut self, provider: &str) {\n        self.failures.insert(provider.to_string(), 0);\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod failure_tracker_tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn Create fresh results\n        let results = ProviderProbeResults {\n            models: std::collections::HashMap::new(),\n            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339(),\n            git_sha: None,\n        };\n\n        // Record failures for multiple providers\n        probe.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        probe.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\"); // Exceeds threshold of 2\n\n        probe.record_failure(\"gcs:hrrr\"); // Below threshold\n\n        probe.record_failure(\"s3:gefs\");\n        probe.record_failure(\"s3:gefs\"); // Exceeds threshold of 2\n\n        probe.record_failure(\"gcs:gefs\"); // Below threshold\n\n        // Verify individual should_reprobe states\n        assert!(probe.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\"), \"s3:hrrr should need reprobe\");\n        assert!(!probe.should_reprobe(\"gcs:hrrr\"), \"gcs:hrrr should not need reprobe\");\n        assert!(probe.should_reprobe(\"s3:gefs\"), \"s3:gefs should need reprobe\");\n fresh results\n        let results = ProviderProbeResults {\n            models: std::collections::HashMap::new(),\n            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339(),\n            git_sha: None,\n        };\n\n        // Simulate consecutive HTTP errors for a provider\n        // Initially is_valid should return true\n        assert!(probe.is_valid(&results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"is_valid should return true initially with no failures\");\n\n        // First HTTP error\n        probe.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        assert!(!probe.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\"), \"should_reprobe should be false after 1 failure\");\n        assert!(probe.is_valid(&results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"is_valid should still be true after 1 failure\");\n\n        // Second HTTP error\n        probe.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        assert!(!probe.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\"), \"should_reprobe should be false after 2 failures\");\n        assert!(probe.is_valid(&results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"is_valid should still be true after 2 failures\");\n\n        // Third HTTP error - this should trigger reprobe\n        probe.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        assert!(probe.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\"), \"should_reprobe should be true after 3 failures\");\n        assert!(!probe.is_valid(&results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"is_valid should be false after 3 consecutive failures\");\n\n        // Verify the consecutive error counter is being tracked correctly\n        assert_eq!(probe.failure_count(\"s3:hrrr\"), 3, \"failure count should be 3\");\n\n        // Simulate a successful request - should reset the counter\n        probe.record_success(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        assert_eq!(probe.failure_count(\"s3:hrrr\"), 0, \"failure count should be reset to 0\");\n        assert!(!probe.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\"), \"should_reprobe should be false after success\");\n        assert!(probe.is_valid(&results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"is_valid should be true after counter is reset\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_is_valid_dual_trigger_logic() {\n        let mut probe = ProviderProbe::new().with_threshold(3);\n\n        // Test that is_valid returns false if EITHER staleness OR should_reprobe is true\n        // (dual-trigger logic: stale OR should_reprobe)\n\n        // Test 1: Fresh results, no failures - should be valid\n        let fresh_results = ProviderProbeResults {\n            models: std::collections::HashMap::new(),\n            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339(),\n            git_sha: None,\n        };\n        assert!(probe.is_valid(&fresh_results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"Fresh results with no failures should be valid\");\n\n        // Test 2: Stale results, no failures - should be invalid (staleness trigger)\n        let stale_results = ProviderProbeResults {\n            models: std::collections::HashMap::new(),\n            timestamp: (chrono::Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::hours(25)).to_rfc3339(),\n            git_sha: None,\n        };\n        assert!(!probe.is_valid(&stale_results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"Stale results should be invalid even with no failures\");\n\n        // Test 3: Fresh results, with failures - should be invalid (should_reprobe trigger)\n        probe.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        probe.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        probe.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        assert!(!probe.is_valid(&fresh_results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"Fresh results with failures should be invalid\");\n\n        // Test 4: Stale results, with failures - should be invalid (both triggers)\n        assert!(!probe.is_valid(&stale_results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"Stale results with failures should be invalid (both triggers active)\");\n\n        // Test 5: Fresh results, with failures below threshold - should be valid\n        let mut probe2 = ProviderProbe::new().with_threshold(5);\n        probe2.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        probe2.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        assert!(probe2.is_valid(&fresh_results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"Fresh results with failures below threshold should be valid\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_should_reprobe_boundary_conditions() {\n        let probe = ProviderProbe::new().with_threshold(3);\n\n        // Test with different thresholds to ensure boundary is handled correctly\n        for threshold in 1..=5 {\n            let mut probe = ProviderProbe::new().with_threshold(threshold);\n\n            // Record (threshold - 1) failures - should NOT trigger reprobe\n            for _ in 0..(threshold - 1) {\n                probe.record_failure(\"test_provider\");\n            }\n            assert!(!probe.should_reprobe(\"test_provider\"),\n                    \"should_reprobe should be false at threshold-1 for threshold={}\", threshold);\n\n            // Record one more failure - should trigger reprobe\n            probe.record_failure(\"test_provider\");\n            assert!(probe.should_reprobe(\"test_provider\"),\n                   \"should_reprobe should be true at exactly threshold for threshold={}\", threshold);\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn }\n\n    /// Record a failure for the given provider\n    ///\n    /// Increments the consecutive failure counter for the provider.\n    /// Returns the current failure count after incrementing.\n    pub fn record_failure(&mut self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n        let count = self.consecutive_failures.entry(provider.to_string()).or_insert(0);\n        *count += 1;\n        *count\n    }\n\n    /// Record a success for the given provider\n    ///\n    /// Resets the consecutive failure counter for the provider to zero.\n    pub fn record_success(&mut self, provider: &str) {\n /// **Dual-trigger logic:**\n    /// 1. **Staleness trigger:** Calls `is_stale()` (lines 402-412) to check if\n    ///    probe data is older than `max_age` (default 24 hours). Returns `false`\n    ///    immediately if stale.\n    ///\n    /// 2. **Failure trigger:** Checks all tracked providers using `should_reprobe()`.\n    ///    Returns `false` if ANY provider has exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    ///\n    /// 3. **Re-probe condition:** Returns `false` if **EITHER** trigger fires:\n    ///    - `is_stale() == true`  (probe data too old)\n    ///    - `any(should_reprobe()) == true` (any provider has too many failures)\n    ///\n    /// This implements the OR logic for the dual-trigger system: staleness OR\n    /// consecutive failures should trigger a re-probe.\n    ///\n    /// **Parallel execution:** Uses `par_iter()` via rayon to check `should_reprobe()`\n    /// for all tracked providers **concurrently**, improving performance when there\n    /// are multiple providers to evaluate. Arguments\n    /// * `results` - The probe results to check for staleness\n    /// * `max_age` - Maximum age for probe results to be considered fresh\n    #[cfg(not(feature = \"rayon\"))]\n    pub fn is_valid(&self, results: &ProviderProbeResults, max_age: Duration) -> bool {\n        // First check staleness\n        if Self::is_stale(results, max_age) {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Then check if any tracked provider has exceeded the failure threshold\n        // Use should_reprobe() for consistency\n        //\n        // INTEGRATION: This is where should_reprobe() is called to implement the\n        // failure-tracking half of the dual-trigger re-probe logic.\n        for provider in self.consecutive_failures.keys() {\n            if self.should_reprobe(provider) {\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n\n        true\n    }\n\n    /// Get providers that need re-probing due to consecutive failures\n    ///\n    /// Returns a list of provider names that have exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    /// This can be used to log which providers are problematic before triggering a re-probe.\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// A vector of provider names that need re-probing\n    pub fn providers_needing_reprobe(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        let mut needing = Vec::new();\n\n        for (provider, &count) in &self.consecutive_failures {\n            if count >= self.consecutive_failure_threshold {\n                needing.push(provider.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        needing\n    }\n\n    /// Get the current consecutive failure count for a provider\n    pub fn failure_count(&self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n        self.consecutive_failures.get(provider).copied().unwrap_or(0)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the consecutive failure threshold\n    pub fn failure_threshold(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.consecutive_failure_threshold\n    }\n\n    /// Reset all failure counters\n    pub fn reset_failures(&mut self) {\n        self.consecutive_failures.clear();\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for ProviderProbe {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Inner result from a single probe\n#[derive(Debug)]\nstruct ProbeInnerResult {\n    connect_time: Duration,\n    ttfb: Duration,\n    throughput_mbs: f64,\n}\n\n/// Runtime tracker for consecutive provider failures\n///\n/// This is a lightweight struct that can be used at runtime to track HTTP request\n/// failures per provider and determine when re-probing is needed. It should be used\n/// alongside the loaded provider-probe.json results.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// This example shows how to use the failure tracker to monitor provider health:\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use gribtract_fetch::probe::ProviderFailureTracker;\n///\n/// // Create a failure tracker with threshold of 3 consecutive errors\n/// let mut tracker = ProviderFailureTracker::new(3);\n///\n/// // Simulate HTTP request results\n/// // tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n/// // tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n/// // tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n///\n/// // Check if re-probing is needed\n/// if tracker.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\") {\n///     println!(\"Provider s3:hrrr needs re-probing due to consecutive failures\");\n/// }\n///\n/// // Reset after successful request\n/// // tracker.record_success(\"s3:hrrr\");\n/// ```\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ProviderFailureTracker {\n    /// Consecutive failure count per provider\n    failures: std::collections::HashMap<String, u32>,\n    /// Threshold for consecutive failures before re-probing\n    threshold: u32,\n}\n\nimpl ProviderFailureTracker {\n    /// Create a new failure tracker with the specified threshold\n    pub fn new(threshold: u32) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            failures: std::collections::HashMap::new(),\n            threshold,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new failure tracker with default threshold (3)\n    pub fn default_threshold() -> Self {\n        Self::new(3)\n    }\n\n    /// Record a failure for the given provider\n    ///\n    /// Returns the current failure count after incrementing.\n    pub fn record_failure(&mut self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n        let count = self.failures.entry(provider.to_string()).or_insert(0);\n        *count += 1;\n        *count\n    }\n\n    /// Record a success for the given provider\n    ///\n    /// Resets the consecutive failure counter for the provider to zero.\n    pub fn record_success(&mut self, provider: &str) {\n        self.failures.insert(provider.to_string(), 0);\n    }\n\n    /// Check if a provider should be re-probed due to consecutive failures\n    ///\n    /// Returns true if the provider has exceeded the consecutive failure threshold.\n    /// This should be checked alongside the staleness check when deciding whether\n    /// to refresh provider probe results.\n    pub fn should_reprobe(&self, provider: &str) -> bool {\n        self.failures\n            .get(provider)\n            .map(|&count| count >= self.threshold)\n            .unwrap_or(false)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the current consecutive failure count for a provider\n    pub fn failure_count(&self, provider: &str) -> u32 {\n        self.failures.get(provider).copied().unwrap_or(0)\n    }\n\n    /// Get the consecutive failure threshold\n    pub fn threshold(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.threshold\n    }\n\n    /// Reset all failure counters (e.g., after re-probing completes)\n    pub fn reset_all(&mut self) {\n        self.failures.clear();\n    }\n\n    /// Reset failure counter for a specific provider\n    pub fn reset_provider(&mut self, provider: &str) {\n        self.failures.insert(provider.to_string(), 0);\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod failure_tracker_tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_failure_tracker_basic() {\n        let mut tracker = ProviderFailureTracker::new(3);\n\n        // Initially, no failures recorded\n        assert_eq!(tracker.failure_count(\"s3:hrrr\"), 0);\n        assert!(!tracker.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\"));\n\n        // Record first failure\n        assert_eq!(tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\"), 1);\n        assert_eq!(tracker.failure_count(\"s3:hrrr\"), 1);\n        assert!(!tracker.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\"));\n\n        // Record second failure\n        assert_eq!(tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\"), 2);\n        assert_eq!(tracker.failure_count(\"s3:hrrr\"), 2);\n        assert!(!tracker.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\"));\n\n        // Record third failure - reaches threshold\n        assert_eq!(tracker.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\"), 3);\n        assert_eq!(tracker.failure_count(\"s3:hrrr\"), 3);\n        assert!(tracker.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\"));\n\n        // Record a success - should reset the counter\n        tracker.record_success(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        assert_eq!(tracker.failure_count(\"s3:hrrr\"), 0);\n        assert!(!tracker.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\"));\n    }\n\n
